## Proof

**Claim:** Yes, $M$ is flat as an $A/I$-module.

**Key isomorphism.** For every $A/I$-module $N$, there is a natural isomorphism of abelian groups
$$N \otimes_{A/I} M \;\cong\; N \otimes_A M.$$

*Proof of the isomorphism.* Since $M$ is annihilated by $I$ (as $IM=0$), the $A$-module structure on $M$ factors through $A/I$, making $M$ an $A/I$-module. Likewise $N$ is an $A/I$-module. The map
$$N \times M \longrightarrow N \otimes_A M, \qquad (n,m)\mapsto n\otimes_A m$$
is $A$-bilinear, and since $I$ acts trivially on both $N$ and $M$, it is in fact $(A/I)$-balanced. Hence by the universal property of the tensor product over $A/I$ it induces a map
$$\varphi: N\otimes_{A/I} M \longrightarrow N\otimes_A M.$$
Conversely, the canonical $A$-bilinear map $N\times M\to N\otimes_{A/I}M$ factors through $N\otimes_A M$ (again because $I$ acts trivially on both sides, so the relations $na\otimes m = n\otimes am$ for $a\in I$ are already trivial in $N\otimes_{A/I}M$), giving a map
$$\psi: N\otimes_A M \longrightarrow N\otimes_{A/I} M.$$
The maps $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are mutually inverse on simple tensors and hence on all elements, establishing the isomorphism. $\square$

(Equivalently, one may compute: $N\otimes_A M \cong N\otimes_{A/I}(A/I\otimes_A M) \cong N\otimes_{A/I} M/IM = N\otimes_{A/I} M$, using $IM=0$.)

**Flatness over $A/I$.** Let
$$0 \longrightarrow N' \longrightarrow N \longrightarrow N'' \longrightarrow 0$$
be any short exact sequence of $A/I$-modules. Every $A/I$-linear map is $A$-linear (via the quotient map $A\to A/I$), and exactness of a sequence of modules is detected at the level of underlying abelian groups, so this is also a short exact sequence of $A$-modules.

Since $M$ is flat as an $A$-module, tensoring over $A$ preserves exactness:
$$0 \longrightarrow N'\otimes_A M \longrightarrow N\otimes_A M \longrightarrow N''\otimes_A M \longrightarrow 0.$$

Applying the key isomorphism to each term (all of $N', N, N''$ are $A/I$-modules), this sequence is canonically identified with
$$0 \longrightarrow N'\otimes_{A/I} M \longrightarrow N\otimes_{A/I} M \longrightarrow N''\otimes_{A/I} M \longrightarrow 0,$$
which is therefore exact.

Since tensoring with $M$ over $A/I$ preserves the exactness of every short exact sequence of $A/I$-modules, $M$ is flat as an $A/I$-module. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE

Hence $M$ is flat over $A/I$.
